# CSCI 435 PR review

You are drafting a code review that the user (GitHub login `ab-wm`) will test, edit and post on a
teammate's PR in `CSCI-435-SE/gitea`, a course fork of Gitea. The review is a graded course
deliverable, so the user stays its author: you gather the facts, check them, and hand back a
draft in their format. Don't post, approve or comment on the PR, and don't push to it. Don't offer
to fix the author's code either. In this course the author makes each change themselves, one
change per commit.

The user's standing instruction for reviews is "not *that* deep". That doesn't mean overlooking
real problems, and it doesn't mean nitpicking every small one. The code is not going upstream. A
finding belongs in the draft only if it would change a score, or if the author would want to know
about it before merging.

## 1. Find your footing

Work out where you are running, because that decides how you fetch the PR and where the draft goes.

- **Claude Code inside the repo clone** (`gh` works, and the working tree is the fork). Use `gh`
  for PR data and read source files locally. The user is usually on their own feature branch, so
  don't switch it. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr-<N>` and read files
  with `git show pr-<N>:<path>`. Compare with `git diff origin/main...pr-<N>`, because local
  `main` is often behind.
- **Chat, or anywhere without the clone.** The repo is public. Use a GitHub connector if one is
  attached. Otherwise fetch the URLs in `references/fetching-without-the-repo.md`. If nothing can
  reach GitHub, ask the user for the PR link and the diff.

## 2. Triage

First get the PR's title, author, changed files and linked issue (`Closes #N`). Then decide how
much review it needs. The user only does a full review when code changed:

- **The PR is already merged, or the user has already reviewed it.** Say so first, quoting their
  existing review in a line. Continue only if they want a fresh look, for example a re-review
  after new commits. Don't let their earlier scores steer yours.
- **The PR only touches check-ins, docs, course files, showcase material, AI logs, or config like
  `.coderabbit.yaml`.** Skip the rubric. Skim the files for anything surprising, such as code
  hiding in a "docs" PR, a secret, or a file in the wrong folder. Then suggest a one-line
  approval in the user's voice, for example "All good, just the check-in doc and AI log. No need
  for complete review."
- **The PR is the user's own.** Nobody approves their own PR in this course. Say so, and offer a
  list of findings instead of a rubric.
- **This is a follow-up after the user asked for changes.** Check only the items they asked for.
  If those are done, suggest a short approval such as "All good now!"
- **The PR changes code or tests.** Do the full review described below.

## 3. Gather, lightly

Read these in order, and stop once you can score every rubric row:

1. The PR description, and the linked issue's acceptance criteria (ACs) and design decisions.
   The rubric is scored against the ACs.
2. The diff. Skip `ai-logs/**`: those files are thousands of lines of chat transcript, and they
   are not reviewed.
3. CodeRabbit's comments and the author's replies, so you don't repeat what was already raised
   and fixed.
4. The CI status, if you can see it.
5. Just enough of the code the diff touches or depends on to check its claims. In the clone,
   `.claude-students/INDEX.md` lists short docs for each area if you need background.

Don't run lint, builds, servers or e2e suites unless the user asks. CI already runs lint and the
tests, and the user does their own hands-on testing. Don't split the review across subagents.

Aim for about 10–15 tool calls on a typical PR. In testing, runs that went to 35 calls produced
no better drafts than shorter ones would have. Spend those calls on checking the findings that
will go in the draft, one check each. Don't chase ideas you won't include. Don't read the
author's AI logs, and only download a library's source when a finding depends on it. If you go
over the budget, write the draft with what you have, and say what you didn't check.

## 4. What to check

- **Each AC.** Find where it is implemented and where it is tested. A missing AC is the main
  reason to lower the Correctness score.
- **Whether the tests can fail.** A test that would still pass with the feature removed doesn't
  count as coverage. Look for:
  - assertions that read a value without first asserting it exists;
  - `test.fail()` or skips that cover more than the one known failure;
  - checks that only test whether something is present.
- **Course rules that graders look at:**
  - a `## Tech Debt` section;
  - an AI assistance section;
  - before/after screenshots when templates, CSS or Vue files change;
  - Conventional Commit messages that end in `(#N)`;
  - `Assisted-by` trailers, and no `Co-Authored-By`;
  - commits small enough to review, for example split by layer.

  If you are unsure of the current sprint's rules, read `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, or
  fetch it.
- **Claims in the PR description.** Descriptions are often drafted by AI. Check one or two
  concrete claims against the code, such as a timing, a count, or "every test does X".

Check every finding against the source before it goes in the draft. Reviews of AI-written code
tend to produce confident findings that turn out wrong. A wrong finding in a posted review costs
the user more than a missed nit. If checking disproves your idea, drop the finding or reword it.
For example, on #105 a suspected "silent pass" turned out to fail loudly, so the finding became
about the unhelpful error message instead.

Leave out style nits, anything lint or CI catches, CodeRabbit findings the author already fixed
(credit those in one line), and anything that wouldn't change a score.

## 5. Scoring

Start every row at 10, and deduct points only for a concrete gap you can name. Past reviews show
how the user scores:

- A UI change without before/after screenshots: Documentation 8, Overall 9, "Yes, once the
  screenshots are added".
- One large commit instead of commits split by layer: AI transparency 7.
- A factual error in the description or the Tech Debt section: Documentation 8.
- Everything checks out: 10s, and Overall 10, "Yes".

A deduction needs a *required* point behind it, something you would ask the author to change before
merging. An observation you'd only file under "Strictly optional" (one AC covered by unit tests but not
end to end, a small AI-assisted commit the description doesn't mention) leaves the score at 10. The user
has scored a feature PR 10 on every row even though optional observations like these existed.

Overall is "Yes" unless something required is missing. Nits don't block a merge. Any score below
7 needs a note saying what would raise it, because the course rubric requires one.

## 6. Draft format

Use the rows from the course rubric. Read `.github/code-review-rubric.md` from the repo, or from
raw GitHub, so the draft picks up any change to the rubric. The template below matches the rubric
as of Sprint 2.

Write in the user's voice:

- short, plain sentences;
- one sentence per table note;
- no rule citations in the table;
- `file:line` for code findings.

Skim one of the reviews in `references/posted-examples.md` before you draft. These are reviews
the user actually posted.

```markdown
### Code Review — @ab-wm

TODO (you): what you ran, clicked or checked yourself.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |

### Strictly optional for completeness
**<the point in a few words>.** <one or two sentences, with file:line>

### AI-Log
Review was drafted by AI, and then changed to better fit the review structure and my inspection of the files. Log available on #<linked issue>.
```

- **Required changes** go in the note of the row they affect, written as a request ("please add
  before/after screenshots, as they are required"). Overall then says "Yes, once X is added".
- **Optional points** go in their own section after the table. Keep at most one or two, and drop
  the section if there are none.
- **The testing line** stays a visible `TODO`. It records what the user checked by hand, and they
  write it themselves. Don't fill it with what you did. A visible placeholder can't be posted by
  accident without being noticed.

## 7. Hand it back

- **In Claude Code**, write the draft to `.specstory/pr-<N>-review.md` (the folder is
  gitignored). If that file already exists, it may be the user's edited copy, so write the draft
  to `pr-<N>-review-2.md` (or the next free number) instead.
- **In chat**, give the draft as one fenced markdown block, so the table copies cleanly.

Then write a short summary in chat, about 10–15 lines:

- the verdict;
- each finding, marked required or optional;
- what you checked and what you didn't (for example, "didn't run the e2e suite"), so the user
  can write their testing line;
- any idea you couldn't verify, offered as something the user could try in their own testing.
  Unverified ideas never go in the draft.

End there. Remind the user to file this session's AI log as `ai-logs/README.md` describes, since
the AI-Log section points to it.

## What changed

The Notifications page has a new **Group by repository** button next to the Repository and Type filters. When it is on, the list is split into one section per repository, ordered A–Z, with each section's notifications newest first. Each section header shows the repository name (a link to the repository), its unread count, and "(continued)" when the section started on the previous page. Clicking the header, or pressing Enter or Space on its chevron button, collapses or expands the section.

- **Model** (`models/activities`): `FindNotificationOptions` gets a `GroupByRepo` option. It joins `repository` and orders by `LOWER(owner_name), lower_name, updated_unix DESC, id DESC`, so a repository's rows stay together across pages. The order is case-insensitive like the repository filter's list, and the `id` tiebreak keeps rows from moving between pages. A new `CountNotificationsByRepo` gives the header counts in one `GROUP BY` query.
- **Router** (`routers/web/user/notification.go`): `group=repo` is parsed into the existing `notificationFilter`, so every redirect that already carried `repo` and `source` (purge, bulk actions, the bulk JSON redirect) now carries `group` too. Grouping is a view setting, not a filter, so it doesn't show "Clear filters" or the "no notifications match" message. On page 2 and later, one extra one-row query finds the repository the previous page ended on. A small pure function, `groupNotificationsByRepo`, builds the sections.
- **Templates**: the row markup moved, unchanged, into `templates/user/notification/notification_item.tmpl`. The flat list and the grouped list both use it, so turning grouping off renders the same rows as before. `group` is added to the tab links, filter links, clear-filter links, purge form, single-row status forms and the bulk URL. Pagination already carries it.
- **Frontend**: `web_src/js/features/notification-group.ts` keeps the collapsed repository IDs in a module-level set and re-applies them every time the list is re-rendered. That happens on a live refresh, a single-row action, or a bulk action. Styles are in `web_src/css/user.css`, and 4 new strings are in `locale_en-US.json`.

## Why

Users with notifications from many repositories had to filter to each repository in turn to work through them. Grouping lets them work through one project at a time without leaving the list. This PR covers every acceptance criterion in #117:

- **AC1:** one section per repository, headed by its full name and unread count (hidden at 0), rows newest first.
- **AC2:** sections are ordered A–Z by full name and don't reorder when the list refreshes.
- **AC3:** sorting happens in the query, so each repository is contiguous across pages, and a section that carries over shows "(continued)".
- **AC4:** `group=repo` survives tab switches, both filters, paging, single-row read/pin, bulk actions, "Mark all as read", and the in-place refresh.
- **AC5:** a section header toggles on click, Enter or Space; the chevron button announces `aria-expanded`; collapsed sections stay collapsed when the list re-renders.
- **AC6:** pinned notifications stay inside their repository's section with their pin icon.
- **AC7:** with grouping off, the list renders the same rows in the same order as before.

## How it was tested

### Test strategy

The ordering and counting rules are pure database logic, so they're tested at the model level. Splitting a page into sections is a pure function, so it's unit-tested without a database. Whether every link and redirect keeps `group=repo` can only be seen in the rendered HTML, so that's an integration test. Collapsing, and staying collapsed when the list is swapped out, happens in the browser, so it's covered by a Vitest test plus one Playwright test on a real page.

| AC | Test |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | `TestCountNotificationsByRepo` (counts per repository, under filters); integration `SectionsByRepoNewestFirst` and `UnreadCountCoversTheRepository` (header text, rows per section, no headers when nothing matches) |
| AC2 | `TestFindNotificationsGroupByRepo` (grouped order differs from newest-first and holds across pages) |
| AC3 | `TestGroupNotificationsByRepo` ("continued" only on the first section and only when the previous page ended in the same repository); integration `ContinuedAcrossPages` (page 2 continues, page 3 starts a new repository) |
| AC4 | `TestParseNotificationFilter` and `TestNotificationViewLink` (`group` cases); integration `LinksKeepGrouping`, `InPlaceRefreshKeepsGrouping` and `RedirectsKeepGrouping` (tabs, both filters, pagination, status forms, bulk URL, `div-only`, bulk and purge redirects) |
| AC5 | Vitest `notification-group.test.ts` (button and header toggle, the repository link doesn't toggle, collapse re-applied to new markup); Playwright `notification-group.test.ts` (Enter and Space on the button, a section stays collapsed after a pin re-renders the list) |
| AC6 | `TestGroupNotificationsByRepo` and integration `SectionsByRepoNewestFirst` (pinned #3 inside user2/repo1) |
| AC7 | integration `OffIsUnchanged`; the existing `TestNotificationFilters`, `TestNotificationBulkActions` and `notification-bulk` e2e tests still pass against the extracted row template |

**Not covered automatically:** how the sections look (borders, chevron rotation, header spacing). I checked this by hand with screenshots from a local instance, shown below. Taking them caught a doubled border under a collapsed section, which is fixed in 189512d0d2.

## CI / manual verification

Run in WSL (Debian) on this branch:

- `go test` for `TestFindNotificationsGroupByRepo`, `TestCountNotificationsByRepo` (`./models/activities/`) and `TestGroupNotificationsByRepo`, `TestParseNotificationFilter`, `TestNotificationViewLink` (`./routers/web/user/`): pass.
- `make test-integration#TestNotification`: pass, including all 8 `TestNotificationGroupByRepo` subtests (0.58 s).
- `pnpm exec vitest run` for `notification-group.test.ts` (3) and `notification-bulk.test.ts` (7): 10/10 pass.
- Playwright `notification-group.test.ts` and `notification-bulk.test.ts` on Chromium and Firefox: 4/4 pass. The grouping test takes about 3 s, which is above the 2 s target; most of that is creating the user, repositories and issues and waiting for the notification queue, the same setup cost as the existing bulk test.
- `make lint-go lint-js lint-css lint-templates lint-editorconfig`: clean.
- CI runs on this PR and must pass before merging.

## Design

The four design decisions are in #117: sort by repository in the query (Decision 1), A–Z section order (Decision 2), grouping kept in the URL like the #50 filters (Decision 3), and collapsed sections kept in page memory (Decision 4, added during implementation along with the answers to both Open Questions).

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** A grouped page after the first runs one extra one-row query to find the repository the previous page ended on, so a carried-over section can say "(continued)". It is cheap, but it repeats the ordered query with the repository join. Collapsed sections live in page memory, so they reopen on paging or leaving the page; this is the trade-off chosen in Decision 4.

**Encountered:** The pager counts only the tab's status (unread or read), but the list also shows pinned notifications. When pinned rows push the list past the last page, the rows at the end can't be reached, grouped or not. This was already there, so I left it out of #117's scope; the paging integration test inserts its own unread row so all three pages exist. It's worth its own bug issue.

Group notifications by repository
Part of #7. Builds on #50 (filter by repository and type) and #51 (bulk actions). Upstream request: go-gitea/gitea#9605.

### User Story

As a user who gets notifications from many repositories, I want to group my notification list by repository so that I can work through one project at a time without filtering to each repository in turn.

### User Scenario

Priya has 45 unread notifications spread across `org/backend`, `org/frontend` and `org/docs`. On the Notifications page she picks "Group by repository". The list turns into one section per repository, each headed by the repository name and its unread count, with that repository's notifications newest first. She collapses `org/docs` to deal with it later, works through `org/backend`, and marks its rows read with the bulk bar from #51. The grouping stays on as the list refreshes and when she moves to page 2, and the URL keeps it, so her bookmark opens the grouped view next time.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given notifications from at least two repositories, when the user selects "Group by repository", then the list shows one section per repository, each headed by the repository's full name and its unread notification count, with the section's rows ordered newest first. The count is the repository's unread notifications under the current filters, across every page and on either tab, and it is hidden when it is 0.
- [ ] AC2: Given grouping is on, when the list loads, then the sections are ordered by repository full name A–Z, and the order does not change when a new notification arrives and the list refreshes.
- [ ] AC3: Given grouping is on and there are more notifications than fit on one page, when the user moves between pages, then every repository's notifications are contiguous, and a section that continues from the previous page repeats its header marked "(continued)".
- [ ] AC4: Given grouping is on, when the user switches between the Unread and Read tabs, changes the #50 repository or type filter, pages, marks a single notification read or pinned, or runs a #51 bulk action, then grouping is still on afterwards (`group=repo` is kept in the URL), and the in-place list refresh keeps it too.
- [ ] AC5: Given grouping is on, when the user activates a section header with the mouse, Enter or Space, then that section collapses or expands, and screen readers announce whether it is expanded. A collapsed section stays collapsed when the list refreshes in place.
- [ ] AC6: Given a pinned notification, when grouping is on, then it is listed inside its repository's section with its pin icon, not in a separate section.
- [ ] AC7: Given grouping is off (the default), when the page loads, then the list looks and behaves exactly as it does today: newest first, no section headers.

### Out of Scope

- Grouping by type or by reason. Reason needs a schema change and stays in #52.
- Per-section actions, such as "Mark this repository as read". The #50 repository filter plus "Mark all as read" already covers this.
- Remembering the grouping choice or collapsed sections between visits, other than through the URL.
- Changes to the notifications API (`/api/v1/notifications`).

### Open Questions

- ~~Should the section header link to the repository?~~ Decided: yes. The name is a link, and the rest of the header toggles the section.
- ~~Should "Select page" in the bulk bar also get a per-section checkbox?~~ Decided: no. "Select page" selects every row on the page, including rows in collapsed sections, as in #51.

### Design Decisions

#### Decision 1: Order grouped notifications by repository in the query, not on the page

**Decision:** When grouping is on, the list query sorts by repository full name and then newest first, and pagination stays at 20 rows per page.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Keep the newest-first query and group only the 20 rows already on the page. This is simplest, but one repository shows up on every page in a different spot, which defeats grouping. (b) Turn pagination off when grouping is on, so every group is complete on one page. This is unbounded for users with thousands of read notifications.
**Rationale:** Sorting in the query is the only option that keeps each repository together across pages while keeping page size bounded.
**Consequences:** The notification find options need a sort option, because the order is fixed to `updated_unix DESC` today, and the sort needs a join on the repository. A group can be split across a page boundary, which AC3's "(continued)" header handles.

#### Decision 2: Sections are ordered A–Z, not by most recent activity

**Decision:** Repository sections are ordered alphabetically by full name.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Order sections by each repository's newest notification, like the ungrouped list. (b) Order by unread count, highest first.
**Rationale:** The list refreshes in place whenever the unread count changes, so with (a) or (b) the sections would jump around while the user is reading or selecting rows. Alphabetical order stays put, and the user can find a repository where they expect it.
**Consequences:** A busy repository late in the alphabet can sit on page 2 or later. The #50 repository filter is the way to jump straight to it.

#### Decision 3: The grouping choice lives in the URL, like the #50 filters

**Decision:** Grouping is a `group=repo` query parameter, carried through every link, form and refresh the filters already carry.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Save it as a per-user setting on the server. (b) Save it in the browser's local storage.
**Rationale:** It matches #50's decision that filters live in the URL: bookmarkable, shareable, and it comes back clean when the user leaves the page. A server setting adds a settings page entry and a write on every toggle for a view preference. Local storage would be invisible to the server-rendered page and the `div-only` refresh.
**Consequences:** Every place that rebuilds the notifications URL (tab links, filter links, pagination, single-row status actions, bulk actions, `div-only` refresh, redirects) has to carry `group`, which is the same set of places #50 changed for `repo` and `source`.

#### Decision 4: Collapsed sections are kept in page memory

**Decision:** The page remembers which sections are collapsed in JavaScript memory and re-applies it whenever the list refreshes in place.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Keep the collapsed sections in the URL, for example `collapsed=1,2`, like `group=repo`. (b) Remember nothing, so a refresh expands every section again.
**Rationale:** The list refreshes in place whenever the unread count changes, and that replaces the whole list, so with (b) a section the user collapsed would reopen while they work, which breaks the user scenario. (a) would survive paging and bookmarks, but every link, form and redirect that already carries `repo`, `source` and `group` would have to carry one more parameter, for a preference the Out of Scope section already says is not remembered between visits.
**Consequences:** Collapsed sections reopen when the user moves to another page or leaves the notifications page. Keeping them across pages would mean moving to (a) later.

### Scope

medium

+func CountNotificationsByRepo(ctx context.Context, opts FindNotificationOptions) (map[int64]int64, error) {

+		RepoID int64
+		Count  int64
+	}, 0, 10)

+		Where(opts.ToConds()).
+		GroupBy("notification.repo_id").

+// notificationGroup is one repository's section of the grouped notification list
+type notificationGroup struct {
+	Repo          *repo_model.Repository
+	UnreadCount   int64 // across every page of the view, not only this one
+	Continued     bool  // the section started on the previous page
+	Notifications activities_model.NotificationList
+}
+
+// groupNotificationsByRepo splits a page already ordered by repository into one section per repository
+func groupNotificationsByRepo(notifications activities_model.NotificationList, prevPageRepoID int64, unreadCounts map[int64]int64) []*notificationGroup {
+	groups := make([]*notificationGroup, 0, 4)
+	for _, n := range notifications {
+		if len(groups) == 0 || groups[len(groups)-1].Repo.ID != n.RepoID {
+			groups = append(groups, &notificationGroup{
+				Repo:        n.Repository,
+				UnreadCount: unreadCounts[n.RepoID],
+				Continued:   len(groups) == 0 && n.RepoID == prevPageRepoID,
+			})
+		}
+		last := groups[len(groups)-1]
+		last.Notifications = append(last.Notifications, n)
+	}
+	return groups
+}

+import {initNotificationGroups} from './notification-group.ts';
+import {createElementFromHTML} from '../utils/dom.ts';
+
+// the grouped markup notification_div.tmpl renders; the collapsed state is module-wide, so each test uses its own repo IDs
+function createGroupedTable(repoIDs: string[]) {
+  const table = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>(`
+    <div id="notification_table">
+      ${repoIDs.map((id) => `
+        <div class="notification-group" data-repo-id="${id}">
+          <div class="notification-group-header">
+            <button type="button" class="notification-group-toggle" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="rows-${id}"></button>
+            <a href="/owner/repo${id}">owner/repo${id}</a>
+            <span class="ui label">1 unread</span>
+          </div>
+          <div class="notification-group-rows" id="rows-${id}"><div class="notifications-item"></div></div>
+        </div>`).join('')}
+    </div>`);
+  initNotificationGroups(table);
+  const group = (id: string) => {
+    const el = table.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`.notification-group[data-repo-id="${CSS.escape(id)}"]`)!;
+    return {
+      toggle: el.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.notification-group-toggle')!,
+      link: el.querySelector<HTMLAnchorElement>('a')!,
+      label: el.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.ui.label')!,
+      rows: el.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.notification-group-rows')!,
+    };
+  };
+  return {group};
+}
+
+test('#117 AC5 the header button collapses and expands its section', () => {
+  const {group} = createGroupedTable(['1', '2']);
+  group('1').toggle.click(); // Enter and Space on a button also fire click
+  expect(group('1').toggle.getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('false');
+  expect(group('1').rows.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(true);
+  expect(group('2').toggle.getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('true'); // other sections are untouched
+
+  group('1').label.click(); // the rest of the header toggles too
+  expect(group('1').toggle.getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('true');
+  expect(group('1').rows.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(false);
+});
+
+test('#117 the repository link in the header does not toggle the section', () => {
+  const {group} = createGroupedTable(['3']);
+  group('3').link.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.preventDefault()); // happy-dom would try to navigate
+  group('3').link.click();
+  expect(group('3').toggle.getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('true');
+});
+
+test('#117 AC5 a collapsed section stays collapsed when the list is refreshed in place', () => {
+  const before = createGroupedTable(['4', '5']);
+  before.group('4').toggle.click();
+
+  const after = createGroupedTable(['4', '5']); // the live refresh swaps in freshly rendered markup
+  expect(after.group('4').toggle.getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('false');
+  expect(after.group('4').rows.classList.contains('tw-hidden')).toBe(true);
+  expect(after.group('5').toggle.getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('true');
+});

+import {toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';
+import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from '../modules/observer.ts';
+
+// module state outlives the #notification_div that live refreshes swap in, so a collapsed section stays collapsed;
+// it is gone after leaving or paging, which the spec leaves out of scope
+const collapsedRepoIDs = new Set<string>();
+
+function setCollapsed(group: HTMLElement, collapsed: boolean) {
+  group.querySelector('.notification-group-toggle')!.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!collapsed));
+  toggleElem(group.querySelector('.notification-group-rows')!, !collapsed);
+}
+
+// initNotificationGroups runs for every grouped #notification_table, including the ones swapped in by live refreshes
+export function initNotificationGroups(table: HTMLElement) {
+  for (const group of table.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.notification-group')) {
+    const repoID = group.getAttribute('data-repo-id')!;
+    setCollapsed(group, collapsedRepoIDs.has(repoID));
+    group.querySelector('.notification-group-header')!.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
+      if ((e.target as Element).closest('a')) return; // the repository name is a link
+      const collapsed = !collapsedRepoIDs.has(repoID);
+      if (collapsed) {
+        collapsedRepoIDs.add(repoID);
+      } else {
+        collapsedRepoIDs.delete(repoID);
+      }
+      setCollapsed(group, collapsed);
+    });
+  }
+}
+
+export function initNotificationGroup() {
+  registerGlobalInitFunc('initNotificationGroups', initNotificationGroups);
+}

	if err != nil {

	unreadOpts := filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID)
	unreadOpts.Status = []activities_model.NotificationStatus{activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread}
	filteredUnreadCount, err := db.Count[activities_model.Notification](ctx, unreadOpts) // the navbar badge stays global
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("ErrGetNotificationCount", err)
		return
	}

	viewOpts := filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID)
	viewOpts.Status = []activities_model.NotificationStatus{queryStatus, activities_model.NotificationStatusPinned}
	viewCount, err := db.Count[activities_model.Notification](ctx, viewOpts) // what "select all in this view" acts on
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("ErrGetNotificationCount", err)
		return
	}

	filterRepos, unreadRepoIDs, err := loadNotificationFilterRepos(ctx, ctx.Doer)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("loadNotificationFilterRepos", err)
		return
	}

	pager := context.NewPagination(total, perPage, page, 5)
	if pager.Paginater.Current() < page {
		// use the last page if the requested page is more than total pages
		page = pager.Paginater.Current()
		pager = context.NewPagination(total, perPage, page, 5)
	}

	findOpts := filter.findOptions(ctx.Doer.ID) // pinned rows are filtered like the rest
	findOpts.ListOptions = db.ListOptions{
		PageSize: perPage,
		Page:     page,
	}
	findOpts.Status = []activities_model.NotificationStatus{queryStatus, activities_model.NotificationStatusPinned}
	findOpts.GroupByRepo = filter.GroupByRepo
	nls, err := db.Find[activities_model.Notification](ctx, findOpts)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("db.Find[activities_model.Notification]", err)
		return
	}

	var prevPageRepoID int64 // the repository of the previous page's last row, to mark a section that continues
	var groupUnreadCounts map[int64]int64
	if filter.GroupByRepo {
		if page > 1 {
			prevOpts := findOpts
			prevOpts.ListOptions = db.ListOptions{PageSize: 1, Page: (page - 1) * perPage} // the row just before this page
			prev, err := db.Find[activities_model.Notification](ctx, prevOpts)
			if err != nil {
				ctx.ServerError("db.Find[activities_model.Notification]", err)
				return
			}
			if len(prev) > 0 {
				prevPageRepoID = prev[0].RepoID
			}
		}
		if groupUnreadCounts, err = activities_model.CountNotificationsByRepo(ctx, unreadOpts); err != nil {
			ctx.ServerError("CountNotificationsByRepo", err)
			return
		}
	}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	activities_model "gitea.dev/models/activities"
	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	"gitea.dev/modules/test"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestNotificationGroupByRepo(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	// user2 fixtures: #3 pinned (repo 1), #4 unread (repo 1), #5 unread (repo 2), #2 read (repo 1); #5 is the newest
	session := loginUser(t, "user2")

	type section struct {
		Header string
		IDs    []string
	}
	sectionsAt := func(t *testing.T, link string) ([]section, *HTMLDoc) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", link), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		var sections []section
		doc.doc.Find("#notification_table .notification-group").Each(func(_ int, g *goquery.Selection) {
			s := section{Header: strings.Join(strings.Fields(g.Find(".notification-group-header").Text()), " ")}
			g.Find(".notifications-item").Each(func(_ int, row *goquery.Selection) {
				s.IDs = append(s.IDs, row.AttrOr("id", ""))
			})
			sections = append(sections, s)
		})
		return sections, doc
	}

	t.Run("SectionsByRepoNewestFirst", func(t *testing.T) {
		sections, _ := sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?group=repo")
		assert.Equal(t, []section{
			{"user2/repo1 1 unread", []string{"notification_4", "notification_3"}}, // the pinned row stays in its repository
			{"user2/repo2 1 unread", []string{"notification_5"}},
		}, sections)
	})

	t.Run("OffIsUnchanged", func(t *testing.T) {
		sections, doc := sectionsAt(t, "/notifications")
		assert.Empty(t, sections)
		var ids []string
		doc.doc.Find("#notification_table .notifications-item").Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
			ids = append(ids, s.AttrOr("id", ""))
		})
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"notification_5", "notification_4", "notification_3"}, ids)
	})

	t.Run("UnreadCountCoversTheRepository", func(t *testing.T) {
		sections, _ := sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?type=read&group=repo")
		assert.Equal(t, []section{{"user2/repo1 1 unread", []string{"notification_3", "notification_2"}}}, sections) // #4 is unread, though listed on the other tab

		sections, _ = sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?group=repo&source=commit")
		assert.Empty(t, sections) // nothing matches, so no headers either
	})

	t.Run("ContinuedAcrossPages", func(t *testing.T) {
		// a third unread row makes three pages of one, since the pager counts unread rows only and pinned #3 is extra
		extra := &activities_model.Notification{UserID: 2, RepoID: 2, Status: activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread, Source: activities_model.NotificationSourceRepository, UpdatedBy: 1}
		require.NoError(t, db.Insert(t.Context(), extra))
		defer func() {
			_, err := db.DeleteByID[activities_model.Notification](t.Context(), extra.ID)
			assert.NoError(t, err)
		}()
		extraID := fmt.Sprintf("notification_%d", extra.ID) // the newest row, so it leads user2/repo2

		sections, _ := sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?group=repo&perPage=1&page=2")
		assert.Equal(t, []section{{"user2/repo1 (continued) 1 unread", []string{"notification_3"}}}, sections)

		sections, _ = sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?group=repo&perPage=1&page=3")
		assert.Equal(t, []section{{"user2/repo2 2 unread", []string{extraID}}}, sections) // the previous page ended in another repository
	})

	t.Run("LinksKeepGrouping", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, doc := sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?group=repo&source=issue&perPage=1") // two pages, so there are pagination links
		for _, c := range []struct{ selector, attr string }{
			{".small-menu-items a.item", "href"}, // Unread and Read tabs
			{`[data-test-id="notification-filter-repo"] .menu a.item`, "href"},
			{`[data-test-id="notification-filter-type"] .menu a.item`, "href"},
			{".pagination a.item[href]", "href"},
			{"form.notifications-buttons", "action"}, // single-row status actions
			{"#notification_div", "data-bulk-url"},
		} {
			found := doc.doc.Find(c.selector)
			require.NotZero(t, found.Length(), c.selector)
			found.Each(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) {
				assert.Contains(t, s.AttrOr(c.attr, ""), "group=repo", c.selector)
			})
		}
		clearFilters := doc.doc.Find(".flex-text-block a.ui.button").FilterFunction(func(_ int, s *goquery.Selection) bool {
			return strings.TrimSpace(s.Text()) == "Clear filters"
		})
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?group=repo", clearFilters.AttrOr("href", ""))
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?source=issue", doc.doc.Find(`[data-test-id="notification-group-repo"]`).AttrOr("href", "")) // the toggle turns it off
	})

	t.Run("ToggleTurnsItOn", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, doc := sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?type=read&source=issue")
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?type=read&source=issue&group=repo", doc.doc.Find(`[data-test-id="notification-group-repo"]`).AttrOr("href", ""))
	})

	t.Run("InPlaceRefreshKeepsGrouping", func(t *testing.T) {
		sections, _ := sectionsAt(t, "/notifications?group=repo&div-only=true")
		assert.Len(t, sections, 2)

		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", "/notifications/status?type=unread&page=1&group=repo", map[string]string{
			"notification_id":     "4",
			"notification_action": "pin",
		}), http.StatusOK)
		assert.Equal(t, 2, NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body).doc.Find("#notification_table .notification-group").Length())
	})

	t.Run("RedirectsKeepGrouping", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", "/notifications/bulk?type=read&group=repo", map[string]string{
			"action":           "mark_as_unread",
			"notification_ids": "2",
		}), http.StatusOK)
		redirect := test.ParseJSONRedirect(resp.Body.Bytes()).Redirect
		require.NotNil(t, redirect)
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?group=repo&type=read", *redirect)

		resp = session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "POST", "/notifications/purge?group=repo"), http.StatusSeeOther)
		assert.Equal(t, "/notifications?group=repo", test.RedirectURL(resp))
	})
}
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import {apiCreateRepo, apiCreateIssue, apiCreateUser, apiDeleteUser, apiUserHeaders, loginUser, randomString} from './utils.ts';

test('collapse a repository section by keyboard and keep it collapsed when the list re-renders', async ({page, request}) => {
  const owner = `e2e-group-${randomString(8)}`; // a fresh user, so no other test's notifications are listed
  await apiCreateUser(request, owner);
  await Promise.all(['alpha', 'beta'].map((name) => apiCreateRepo(request, {name, headers: apiUserHeaders(owner)})));
  // the admin's issues notify the owner, who watches their own repos
  await Promise.all([
    apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo: 'alpha', title: 'Alpha notification'}),
    apiCreateIssue(request, {owner, repo: 'beta', title: 'Beta notification'}),
    loginUser(page, owner),
  ]);

  const groups = page.locator('#notification_table .notification-group');
  await expect(async () => { // notifications are written by a background queue
    await page.goto('/notifications?group=repo');
    await expect(groups).toHaveCount(2, {timeout: 500});
  }).toPass();

  const alpha = groups.filter({hasText: `${owner}/alpha`});
  const beta = groups.filter({hasText: `${owner}/beta`});
  const alphaToggle = alpha.locator('.notification-group-toggle');
  const betaToggle = beta.locator('.notification-group-toggle');

  await alphaToggle.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(alphaToggle).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  await expect(alpha.locator('.notifications-item')).toBeHidden();
  await page.keyboard.press('Space');
  await expect(alphaToggle).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  await expect(alpha.locator('.notifications-item')).toBeVisible();

  await betaToggle.click();
  await expect(betaToggle).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // pinning a row re-renders the whole list in place, like a live refresh
  const alphaRow = alpha.locator('.notifications-item');
  await alphaRow.hover();
  await Promise.all([
    page.waitForResponse((response) => response.url().includes('/notifications/status')),
    alphaRow.locator('button[value="pin"]').click(),
  ]);
  await expect(alpha.locator('.notifications-item .octicon-pin.tw-text-blue')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/group=repo/);
  await expect(betaToggle).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  await expect(beta.locator('.notifications-item')).toBeHidden();

  await apiDeleteUser(request, owner);
});

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality including the Tech Debt section 4, CI or manual verification 3,
review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.
----TEMPLATE
----117 comments
[vvchopra 2026-10-26T15:47:25Z] Spec reviewed and approved. The ACs are testable, and the goal is clear. Continue with implementation.
---
